mainTopic: Why a סוטה has no יבום, and רב ששת's rule that the bitter water does not test a woman with witnesses overseas
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of why a סוטה is not taken in יבום. A second version of רב יוסף reads the word "אחר" as a criticism of the man who marries her. רבא gives a קל וחומר instead: if the suspicion forbids her to her own husband, she is surely forbidden to his brother. אביי tests this קל וחומר with a כהן גדול's widow and then with a כהן's raped wife, and the גמרא shows why neither case fits. Next, a new משנה lists five suspected wives of a כהן who may not eat תרומה. רב ששת learns from it that the bitter water does not test a woman who has witnesses overseas. רב יוסף disagrees, saying her merit may have held off the punishment, and the גמרא ties their argument to רבי's idea of 'wasting away.' רב שימי בר אשי challenges רב ששת using רבי שמעון's worry about giving pure women a bad name, and the גמרא answers that רב ששת does not follow רבי שמעון. Finally, רב begins a new challenge from a משנה about women whose meal-offerings are burned, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No man is forced to marry her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier line of discussion with a rhetorical question: do we ever force a man to marry this woman against his will?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we force her on him against his will?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion with a sharp question. An ordinary man who marries this woman does so by his own choice, so the verse is not ordering anyone to take her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יבום, the brother is obligated to marry the widow, so in a sense she is imposed on him. Nobody is obligated to marry a divorced סוטה. So a verse about her marrying "another man" cannot be read as a command that someone must take her.

keyTerms.meaning: marriage of a childless widow to her late husband's brother

phrases.english: Do we impose her
on him against his will?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָא רָמֵינַן לַהּ עֲלֵיהּ בְּעַל כֻּרְחֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument that came just before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the verse as an instruction that some man must marry her.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Unlike a יבם, an ordinary man has no obligation to marry her, so nothing is imposed on him.

steps.title: Second version of רב יוסף: the second husband is called "another"
steps.stepSummary: Others report רב יוסף differently. The תורה calls the man who marries a divorced סוטה "another" to show that he is not the equal of the first husband. So how could she be taken in יבום?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב יוסף said: The verse calls him "another" because he is not the equal of the first husband. The first one sent a wicked woman out of his house, and this one brought a wicked woman into his house. And you are saying she should also have יבום?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רב יוסף's teaching. He reads the word "אחר" (another) as a criticism of the man who marries her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first husband did well by sending away a wicked woman. The second husband did badly by bringing her in, and the תורה hints at this by calling him "another." If even freely marrying her is frowned upon, it makes no sense that the תורה would require a יבם to marry her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the reading of "אחר" that אביי challenges in the next step.

phrases.english: And there are those who say: Rav Yosef said:
The verse calls him "another,"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:2

phrases.english: because he is not the equal of the first husband.
For this one sent a wicked woman out of his house,
and that one brought a wicked woman into his house,
and you say she should also go through יבום?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב יוסף's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word "אחר" shows that marrying a divorced סוטה is looked down on, so a סוטה cannot be required to have יבום.

steps.title: אביי: then a second husband's brother could never do יבום
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. If being called "another" rules out יבום, then if this woman marries a second husband who dies childless, she could never have יבום with his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, if she married another man and he died without children, she should not have יבום, since the verse calls him "another"!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's reasoning by showing where it would lead. It would produce a result nobody accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף tied the ban on יבום to the label "another." But that same label belongs to her second husband. So it should also block יבום with the second husband's brother, which is clearly not the halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: if that is so (a formula that pushes an argument to an absurd result)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two husbands. אביי is not talking about the first husband's brother. He means the brother of the second husband, the one called "another."

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: If that is so,
if she married another man and he died without children,
she should not have יבום,
since the verse calls him "another"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reading from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the word "אחר" rules out יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same label applies to the second husband, so his brother could never do יבום either, which is clearly not the halacha.

steps.title: With the second husband she kept a good name
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that during her marriage to the second husband she behaved properly, so nothing stops יבום with his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: With this one, at least, she kept a good name.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself by pointing to a difference between the two marriages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on יבום comes from her bad reputation in the marriage where she was suspected. In the second marriage nothing bad happened, so she has יבום with the second husband's brother as normal. Only the first husband's family is affected.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, יבום is blocked only in the marriage where she was suspected. In a later marriage where she kept a good name, יבום applies normally.

phrases.english: With this one, at least,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the second husband.

phrases.english: she remained with a good name.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּיהּ דְּהַאי מִיהָא בְּשֵׁם טוֹב הֲוָה קָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word "אחר" blocks יבום in any marriage after the first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the marriage where she was suspected blocks יבום. In the second marriage she had a good name, so יבום works.

steps.title: רבא's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different source using a קל וחומר. If suspicion forbids her to her husband, who was permitted to her, it surely forbids her to his brother, who was already forbidden to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a קל וחומר. If she became forbidden to the one who was permitted to her, then to the one who was forbidden to her, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own reason, built on logic instead of the word "אחר."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her husband was fully permitted to her, yet the suspicion made her forbidden to him. Her husband's brother was forbidden to her to begin with. So the suspicion should certainly keep her forbidden to the brother, and יבום cannot happen.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stronger one (a fortiori)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא learns that a סוטה has no יבום through a קל וחומר: from the husband, who was permitted, to the brother-in-law, who was forbidden.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is an a fortiori argument:
If she became forbidden to the one permitted to her,
phrases.notes: This is her husband.

phrases.english: then to the one forbidden to her, is it not all the more so?
phrases.notes: This is the husband's brother, who was forbidden to her while the husband was alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source from רב יוסף's reading of "אחר."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוטה is forbidden to the יבם by קל וחומר, since she is forbidden even to her own husband, who was permitted to her.

steps.title: אביי tests the reasoning with a כהן גדול's widow
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא's קל וחומר. A כהן גדול was מקדש a widow and died, and his brother is a כהן הדיוט. The same reasoning would forbid יבום here too, which is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, take a כהן גדול who was מקדש a widow and died, and he has a brother who is a regular כהן. By your logic she should not have יבום: if she is forbidden to the one 'permitted' to her, surely she is forbidden to the one who was forbidden to her!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's קל וחומר by plugging in a different case, where the same logic gives a result we know is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may not marry a widow, so this widow is forbidden to her husband. His brother, a כהן הדיוט, was forbidden to her while the husband lived, since she was his brother's wife. If רבא's reasoning were sound, it would block יבום here too. אביי's point is that the logic proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: "But according to this..." It introduces a strange result that follows from someone's reasoning.
The High Priest. He may not marry a widow.
A regular כהן, who is allowed to marry a widow.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, who just gave the קל וחומר in the previous step.

phrases.english: But if so,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ אֶת הָאַלְמָנָה וָמֵת,
phrases.english: a High Priest who betrothed a widow and died,
and he has a brother who is a regular priest,
she should not be able to have levirate marriage:
if she is forbidden to the one permitted to her,
then to the one forbidden to her, all the more so?!
phrases.notes: "Forbidden to her" means the brother. While the husband was alive, she was his brother's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's קל וחומר from step 5 with a counter-case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's קל וחומר: forbidden to the permitted husband, so surely forbidden to the forbidden brother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning would wrongly forbid יבום for the widow of a כהן גדול with a כהן הדיוט brother, so the reasoning must be flawed.

steps.title: The High Priest case does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's counter-case. The widow never 'became' forbidden, since she was forbidden from the start, and the כהן גדול was never 'permitted' to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She became forbidden'? She was forbidden all along! 'Permitted to her'? He is forbidden to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's case. It shows that the case does not match the two key parts of רבא's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's קל וחומר needs a husband who was first permitted and then became forbidden. A widow was always forbidden to a כהן גדול, so neither part fits. That means the case says nothing about רבא's logic.

keyTerms.meaning: She was already forbidden and stays forbidden. Nothing new happened.
"She became forbidden." This implies a change from permitted to forbidden.

phrases.english: "She became forbidden"?! She was forbidden and stays that way!
"Permitted to her"?! He is forbidden to her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counter-case from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the כהן גדול counter-case is rejected. רבא's reasoning stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case lacks both features: a husband who was permitted, and a prohibition that came later.

steps.title: A better challenge: a כהן's raped wife and a חלל brother
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is restated with a case that does fit: a כהן's wife was raped, so she became forbidden to him. He died, and his brother is a חלל. By רבא's logic she should not have יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, take a כהן's wife who was raped, and then he died, and he has a brother who is a חלל. She should not have יבום: if she is forbidden to the one permitted to her, surely she is forbidden to the one who was forbidden to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא swaps in a new counter-case that fixes the problem from the last step. This time she really was permitted to her husband and then became forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's wife who is raped becomes forbidden to him. So here she truly was permitted and then became forbidden, just like a סוטה. Her brother-in-law, a חלל, was forbidden to her as a brother's wife. רבא's קל וחומר would block יבום here, and that seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: She was raped. A כהן's wife becomes forbidden to him because of this.
A son of a כהן whose priestly status is lost because of a flawed lineage. He does not keep the marriage limits of a כהן.

phrases.english: Rather: a priest's wife who was raped, and he died,
and he has a brother who is a disqualified priest,
she should not be able to have levirate marriage.
If she is forbidden to the one permitted to her,
then to the one forbidden to her, all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repairs the failed counter-case from step 6 after step 7 rejected it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the woman was truly permitted and then became forbidden, yet blocking יבום with the חלל brother seems wrong. So the קל וחומר seems to prove too much.

steps.title: Rape only forbids a woman to a כהן, not to a חלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that rape does not forbid a woman to an ordinary ישראל. The חלל brother counts as a ישראל, so for him there is no prohibition at all. That is unlike a סוטה, who is forbidden to any husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: A raped woman is fully permitted to a ישראל. As for this man, the חלל, at any rate there is no prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's קל וחומר. It shows that the raped-wife case is different from a סוטה in a key way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rape only forbids a woman to a כהן because of the special holiness of כהונה. An ordinary ישראל husband may stay with his wife after she is raped. A חלל has the marriage status of a ישראל, so the rape never forbids her to him. A סוטה, by contrast, is forbidden to every husband, so רבא's reasoning still works for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Rape, where the woman did not consent.
"Is fully permitted." The double verb stresses that she is completely allowed.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's קל וחומר stands. It works for a סוטה because her prohibition applies to everyone. A raped woman is forbidden only to a כהן, so that case cannot be compared, and a חלל brother may still do יבום.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a raped woman is forbidden to every husband. The prohibition applies only to a כהן. That is exactly why this case falls apart.

phrases.english: A raped woman is fully permitted to an Israelite,
phrases.notes: He means an ordinary Jewish husband who is not a כהן.

phrases.english: and regarding this one, at any rate,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the חלל brother, who counts as a regular ישראל.

phrases.english: there is no prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and protects רבא's קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the prohibition in the counter-case is limited to כהנים, unlike the סוטה's prohibition, which applies to everyone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The raped כהן's wife seemed to match a סוטה, so the קל וחומר would wrongly forbid יבום with a חלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rape forbids a woman only to a כהן. A חלל counts as a ישראל, so she is not forbidden to him at all. The סוטה is forbidden to all, so רבא's קל וחומר holds.

steps.title: The new משנה: five suspected wives who may not eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five cases where a suspected wife is forbidden to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These women are forbidden to eat תרומה: one who says 'I am defiled to you'; one about whom witnesses came that she is defiled; one who says 'I will not drink'; one whose husband does not want to make her drink; and one whose husband was with her on the way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists five kinds of suspected wives of a כהן who may no longer eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the bitter water will not be used to clear her, either because she admitted, was proven guilty, refused, or the process was stopped. Since nothing clears her, the suspicion stays, and she cannot eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן, which only his household may eat
'I am defiled to you', meaning she admits she was unfaithful
'I will not drink', meaning she refuses the bitter water
To make her drink the bitter water
On the way, meaning while traveling to the בית המקדש for the test

phrases.english: MISHNA
And these women are forbidden from eating תרומה:
phrases.notes: These are wives of a כהן; normally his wife may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: One who says, 'I am defiled to you,'
and one about whom witnesses came saying that she is defiled,
and one who says, 'I will not drink,'
and one whose husband does not want to make her drink,
and one whose husband had relations with her on the way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves away from the יבום discussion of the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five kinds of suspected wives of a כהן lose the right to eat תרומה.

steps.title: רב ששת: the water does not test a woman with faraway witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם reports רב ששת's rule: if there are witnesses to her sin overseas, the bitter water does not test her.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב עמרם said: רב ששת told us this, and he showed us a proof from the משנה. A סוטה who has witnesses in a faraway land, the water does not test her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב ששת. If somewhere in the world there are witnesses who saw her sin, the bitter water will not work on her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water only works where the truth cannot be found out through people. If witnesses exist, even far away, the water does not test her. רב עמרם adds that רב ששת proved this from our משנה; that proof comes in steps 13-14.

keyTerms.meaning: A country overseas, meaning far away
Test or check whether she sinned
He lit up our eyes, meaning he showed us a clear proof

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean she is free. It means the water cannot clear or catch her, so the test is not the way to settle her case.

phrases.english: GEMARA
רב עמרם said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: This matter רב ששת told us,
and he lit up our eyes from our משנה:
phrases.notes: "Lit up our eyes" means רב ששת showed us a proof from our משנה. The proof itself comes a bit later.

phrases.aramaic: סוֹטָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם —
phrases.english: A סוטה who has witnesses in a country overseas —
the water does not test her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִילְּתָא אֲמַר לַן רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with רב ששת's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If witnesses to her sin exist anywhere, even far away, the bitter water does not test her.

steps.title: The source: 'and there is no witness against her'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the water is for a case with no witness, so a woman who has witnesses is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The פסוק says, 'and she was hidden and defiled, and there is no witness against her.' This means there is no one who knows about her. That leaves out this case, since here there is someone who knows about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב ששת's rule is true. It answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה describes the סוטה as having 'no witness.' So the water is only for a woman whose sin nobody knows about. If witnesses exist anywhere, someone does know, so the water is not for her.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says,
'And she was hidden and she was defiled, and there is no witness against her,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13

phrases.english: meaning there is no one who knows about her.
This leaves out this case,
since here there is someone who knows about her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רב ששת's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the water does not test a woman who has witnesses somewhere.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'ועד אין בה' in the פסוק.

steps.title: Setting up the proof: when did the witnesses come?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks when the משנה's witnesses came. If they came before she drank, the law would be too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he showed us a proof from the משנה, which teaches: 'and where witnesses came that she is defiled.' When did the witnesses come? If you say before she drank, she is a זונה! That is obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up רב ששת's proof from the משנה. He asks when the witnesses in the משנה came, and rules out 'before she drank.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If witnesses came before she drank, she is simply a proven sinner. Of course she cannot eat תרומה, so the משנה would not need to teach it. So the משנה must mean a different time, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who had forbidden relations, and so is forbidden to a כֹּהֵן

phrases.english: And he lit up our eyes from our משנה,
for it teaches:
'and where witnesses came about her that she is defiled.'
The witnesses came when?
If we say before she drank —
she is a זונה!
phrases.notes: So of course she can't eat תרומה. The משנה wouldn't need to tell us that.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲתוּ עֵדִים אֵימַת? אִי נֵימָא מִקַּמֵּי דְּתִשְׁתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פסוק, רב ששת now begins his second support, which comes from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what point did the witnesses in the משנה come: before or after she drank?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not before, since then the law would be obvious. The answer comes in step 14.

steps.title: The proof: witnesses after she drank only make sense if the water did not test her
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses must have come after she drank. That only works if the water does not test a woman who has witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is after she drank. If you say the water does not test her, it works well. But if you say the water does test her, then it would be revealed backward that the witnesses are liars!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his proof. The משנה must be talking about witnesses who came after she drank and nothing happened to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the water tested her and she survived, that would show she was innocent. Then the later witnesses would have to be liars, and the משנה could not forbid her. Since the משנה does forbid her, the water must not have tested her, because witnesses existed. That is exactly רב ששת's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת: the bitter water does not test a סוטה who has witnesses anywhere, even far away. The source is 'ועד אין בה'. The support is our משנה, which forbids her even when witnesses come after she drank and was not harmed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the bitter water is not a test of every case. It only works where no human witness exists.

phrases.english: Rather, it is after she drank.
It works if you say
the water does not test her — that is fine.
But if you say
the water does test her —
it would be revealed looking back
phrases.notes: She drank and nothing happened, so the water would have shown she was innocent.

phrases.english: that they are lying witnesses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא אֵין הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתָהּ — שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 and uses the answer to prove רב ששת's rule from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's rule that the water does not test a woman who has witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of witnesses who came after she drank, where she is still forbidden to eat תרומה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The water does test her, but merit may delay the punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects רב ששת's proof. The water can test her, and her survival may be because her merit held off the punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Really, I can tell you the water does test her. And this woman who drank and was fine? Say that her merit held off the punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רב ששת's proof from the משנה. He shows that the משנה can be explained even if the water does test a woman who has witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת argued: if the water tested her, then surviving it would prove the later witnesses are lying, so the משנה could not forbid her תרומה. רב יוסף answers that surviving does not prove she is innocent. Her זכות may simply have delayed the punishment, so the witnesses can still be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to hold on to an idea that was being rejected

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying she is innocent. He is saying the water's effect was delayed, so her survival proves nothing either way.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
phrases.notes: He is talking to רב ששת.

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you
the water does test her,
and this one — say that merit held off [the punishment] for her.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the woman in the משנה who drank, was unharmed, and then witnesses came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רב ששת drew in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not necessarily רב ששת's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that surviving the water shows innocence. But merit could have delayed the punishment.

steps.title: What is the real point of disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב ששת and רב יוסף actually argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks what deeper idea divides רב ששת and רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides could know that merit sometimes holds off the punishment. So the גמרא wants to find the exact point where their views split.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רב ששת and רב יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רב יוסף's answer by asking what the two אמוראים really argue about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact principle behind the argument between רב ששת and רב יוסף.

steps.title: They argue about רבי's 'wasting away'
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about whether she wastes away, as רבי describes in a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About רבי's 'wasting away.' As we learned: רבי says: Merit holds off the punishment of the bitter water. But she does not give birth and does not get healthier. Rather, she keeps wasting away, until in the end she dies that same death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is about the 'wasting away' that רבי describes. It quotes his words from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, merit does not cancel the punishment. It only slows it down. A guilty woman with merit still shows signs: she cannot have children, she does not get healthier, and she slowly fades until she dies the death of a סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The bitter water a סוטה drinks

phrases.english: About Rebbi's 'wasting away.'
As we learned: Rebbi says:
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in this מסכת (סוטה 22a).

phrases.english: Merit holds off [the punishment] of the bitter water,
but she does not give birth and does not get healthier,
rather, she keeps wasting away,
until in the end she dies that same death.
phrases.notes: "That same death" is the death a guilty סוטה dies from the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether a woman whose punishment is delayed visibly wastes away, as רבי describes.

steps.title: Each side's view on wasting away
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds she wastes away according to everyone. רב יוסף holds only רבי says so, while the רבנן say she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת holds: according to both רבי and the רבנן, she wastes away. And רב יוסף holds: according to רבי she wastes away, but according to the רבנן she does not waste away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out each אמורא's position on whether the delayed punishment shows on her body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב ששת, every woman whose punishment is held off visibly fades. So a woman who stays healthy after drinking was truly tested and is innocent, which makes later witnesses false. For רב יוסף, according to the רבנן she shows no sign at all. So staying healthy proves nothing, and the later witnesses can be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument comes down to this: does a guilty woman protected by merit show visible decline? רב ששת says yes, according to all. רב יוסף says only according to רבי.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet holds:
both according to Rebbi and according to the Sages,
she wastes away.
And Rav Yosef holds:
according to Rebbi she wastes away,
according to the Sages she does not waste away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת סָבַר: בֵּין לְרַבִּי וּבֵין לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 17 by laying out each side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת: visible wasting away according to everyone. רב יוסף: only according to רבי, not according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי brings רבי שמעון's warning about defaming pure women
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי quotes רבי שמעון: if merit delays the punishment, the water loses its fear and pure women who drank will be suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי raised an objection: רבי שמעון says: Merit does not hold off the punishment of the bitter water. If you say merit holds it off, you weaken the water in front of all the women who drink it. And you give a bad name to the pure women who drank, because people will say: They were impure, but merit held off their punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי quotes רבי שמעון from the same משנה to challenge one of the two views. The גמרא is setting up an attack, and the full point will come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון rejects the idea that merit delays the punishment. His reason is that it would leave pure women who drank and survived under suspicion. In the next step רב שימי בר אשי takes this same reasoning and turns it against רב ששת's rule about witnesses overseas.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushes aside / weakens (the fear of the water)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון himself holds that merit does not delay the punishment. The challenge comes from his reasoning against those who say it does, not from his own ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: This is from the same משנה where רבי spoke (סוטה 22a).

phrases.english: Merit does not hold off [the punishment] of the bitter water.
And if you say
merit holds off [the punishment] of the bitter water —
you weaken the water
phrases.notes: He means guilty women won't fear the water, since they'll count on their merit to protect them.

phrases.english: in front of all the women who drink.
And you give a bad name
to the pure women who drank,
and people will say:
They were impure,
but merit held off [the punishment] for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to רב ששת's rule from step 11 by quoting רבי שמעון's reasoning from the same משנה where רבי spoke.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's rule that the water does not test a woman who has witnesses overseas.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rejects anything that would leave pure women who survived the water under suspicion. Witnesses overseas would leave them suspected in exactly the same way, so רב ששת's rule should be rejected too.

steps.title: The same problem applies to witnesses overseas
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי applies רבי שמעון's argument to רב ששת's rule. If the water does not test a woman with witnesses overseas, innocent women who drank will still be suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is true that the water does not test a woman who has witnesses overseas, then the same complaint applies: you give a bad name to pure women who drank. People will say they really were impure, and the water did nothing only because there are witnesses about them overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי now explains why he quoted רבי שמעון. The same worry that rules out merit also rules out רב ששת's idea about witnesses overseas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's worry is that pure women who drink and survive should be fully cleared. If something besides innocence could explain their survival, they stay suspected. Witnesses overseas would be exactly that kind of explanation, so רב ששת's rule creates the same problem.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so: introduces the result of accepting someone's view
Giving someone a bad name, defaming
Pure women, meaning they did not sin

phrases.english: And if it is so

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם נָמֵי:
phrases.english: that a woman who has witnesses overseas [is not tested], then here too:
phrases.notes: The גמרא skips the words "the water does not test her." That's רב ששת's view, which is being challenged here.

phrases.english: you give a bad name
to the pure women who drank,
and people will say: they were impure,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם!
phrases.english: but they have witnesses overseas!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא יֵשׁ לָהּ עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the רבי שמעון quote in step 19 challenges רב ששת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's rule that the water does not test a woman with witnesses overseas
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's argument against merit delaying the punishment applies equally to witnesses overseas, since both would leave innocent women suspected.

steps.title: רב ששת does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the challenge only works according to רבי שמעון. He holds that neither merit nor witnesses delay the water's effect, and רב ששת does not follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you saying this according to רבי שמעון? According to רבי שמעון, just as merit does not delay the punishment, witnesses do not delay it either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב שימי בר אשי's challenge. It agrees that רבי שמעון would reject רב ששת's rule, but says רב ששת follows the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not disagree with the logic of the challenge. It agrees that רבי שמעון treats merit and witnesses the same way and accepts neither. But רבי שמעון's view is one side of a disagreement, and רב ששת can follow the side that lets merit, and witnesses, make a difference.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון treats merit and witnesses overseas the same way: neither one stops the water. רב ששת's rule only works according to those who disagree with רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Are you saying this according to רבי שמעון?
According to רבי שמעון, since merit does not delay [the punishment],
witnesses also do not delay it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenge to one opinion (רבי שמעון), which רב ששת does not follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's argument seemed to disprove רב ששת's rule for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument only works according to רבי שמעון, who rejects both merit and witnesses as reasons the water might not work. רב ששת follows the other view.

steps.title: רב opens a challenge from the women whose מנחות are burned
steps.stepSummary: רב begins a new challenge. He quotes the opening of a משנה listing women whose meal-offerings are burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב raises a challenge: And these are the women whose meal-offerings are burned.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב starts quoting a משנה that he will use to challenge the view about witnesses overseas, and the rest of the quote comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מֵתִיב means a challenge is coming from a source with authority. For now we only have the heading of the list. The actual difficulty will become clear once the cases on the list are quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal-offering; a סוטה brings one before she drinks
Are burned, instead of being offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: רב raises a challenge:
And these are the women whose meal-offerings are burned,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 21 settles רב שימי בר אשי's challenge, a new challenge from a משנה begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view about women with witnesses overseas (to be made clear as the משנה is quoted)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the challenge will come from the cases listed in the משנה about burned meal-offerings.
